title: BGN with a NON-MONOTONE exposure across a visible level ladder: five types, cash-flow level [0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4], loadings [-0.07, 0.0, 0.07, 0.0, -0.07] (hump-shaped), 21-node chain, exact compensation, price 2.5
question: Does a premium that is hump-shaped across a monotonically visible level ladder give the oracle room in BGN, as the hump in KP14's vyg25s does, and does a gap follow?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-29). In BGN every channel that reveals the loading b (the compensated level theta_b through roe, the uncompensated value through size and bm) reveals it MONOTONICALLY, and the premium is monotone in b, so the linear ceiling captures it: bvychs room 20%, bvychs18/25/n5 no hump (hump_decomp.py). KP14's room came from a premium that is a hump in a monotonically visible b. Here the visible dimension is an explicit cash-flow level ladder (type_level, new parameter: Chat_f = Chat theta_b level_f) and b is arranged non-monotonically across it, so the premium is non-monotone in size and bm by construction. bv_comp 1 equalises project values at y = 0, so size and bm track the ladder alone; roe tracks level x theta_b.

FEASIBILITY (parameters.py + vasicek_vy.py at these overrides, 2026-10-29): theta_b [1, 1.218, 1.477, 1.218, 1], Chat_f = Chat theta_b level_f; values per project at y = 0 proportional to level_f alone. Chain exponents +-0.245.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-29): as bvyvee (room 30-60%), the hump and the V differing only through which types' roe is pulled up by theta_b. FALSIFIED as 'a non-monotone exposure opens room in BGN' if room is at or below bvychs's 20%.
